To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have demonstrated for the first time that the conserved motif of RgpA and of the catalytic domain of Kgp is essential for correct posttranslatal processing and for the assembly of the non-covalent multidomain complexes on the surface of P. gingivalis.
the conserved motif is required for correct proteolytic processing of Kgp, and for assembly of the Kgp catalytic and hemagglutin-adhesion domains into a non-covalent complex.
1) Kgp and RgpA are secreted from the bacteria as complexes with non-covalent interactions, and 2) the conserved motif is important for the correct processing and secretion of the gingipains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and use of new tools to study the role of gingipain complexes in the pathogenicity of P. gingivalis and to understand the mechanisms of gingipain complex formation.
the development of novel strategies for disruption of the gingipain complexes.
the role of the Kgp oligomerization motif in the assembly of the multidimensional Kgp complexes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the conserved motifs function in correct posttranscriptional and posttranslational processing and assembly of gingipain complexes.
the motif functions as an assembly motif, which is required for the correct posttranslitional processing of the multidomain gingipains.
the oligomerization motif is essential in correct posttranscriptional proteolytic processing of the multidomain gingipain complexes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the motif is required for the correct processing and assembly of gingipain complexes, but it is not required for the oligomerization of individual domains.
disruption of the oligomerization motif leads to the secretion of the entire catalytic domain of Kgp, but not RgpA.
disruption of oligomerization by mutation or hexahistidine tagging of the conserved oligomerization motif leads to the secretion of the entire Kgp activity in the culture supernatant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the conserved motif plays an important role in correct posttranscriptional proteolytic processing of the multidomain gingipains.
the oligomerization motif is required for oligomerization and surface attachment of the complexes.
the motif is not involved in oligomerization of the catalytic domain into the complex.
